deals.submarket: Plano / Legacy — Preston Rd & Sam Rayburn Tollway
deals.broker: Newmark Retail Capital Markets (Kyle Minter, James Sharpe V, Conor Lalor, Clint Frease, Andrei Larion; financing: Andrew Porteous, Chris McColpin)
deals.proximityHighways: At the intersection of the Sam Rayburn Tollway / SH-121 (185,000 VPD) and Preston Road (25,000 VPD) — 210,000 VPD combined per the OM — 19 miles north of downtown Dallas.
deals.retailCotenants: Stonebriar Centre (5.1 million annual visits) is one-half mile away; the Property sits adjacent to Legacy Business Park, a 2,665-acre master-planned business/retail/residential community with 36M SF of office and 70,000 residents and employees, anchored by Toyota Motor North America, JPMorgan Chase, PepsiCo and Liberty Mutual.
deals.shadowAnchors: No shadow anchor disclosed. Demand drivers: Legacy Business Park / Legacy West adjacent, Stonebriar Centre 0.5 miles away, and the PGA of America headquarters in Frisco 15 miles north (2027 PGA Championship at PGA Frisco).
deals.notes: **Preston Village** is a **302,993 SF community power center** at 8700 Preston Road in Plano, Texas, on the corner of the **Sam Rayburn Tollway (185,000 VPD) and Preston Road (25,000 VPD)** — 210,000 VPD combined — 19 miles north of downtown Dallas and one-half mile from Stonebriar Centre, adjacent to the 2,665-acre Legacy Business Park. It draws **3.3 million annual visits**. The anchor row is genuinely top-of-market: the **#1 most-visited PGA Tour Superstore in Texas (65,506 SF, of 10 stores)**, the **#1 most-visited HomeGoods in Texas (23,310 SF, of 43)**, **Total Wine & More (28,000 SF)** doing **$36.8 million / $1,313 PSF at a 1.7% occupancy cost**, plus Michaels, World Market, Petco and Pure Hockey — several of them 27-year tenants — and four separately parceled pads (McDonald's since 1998, Dimassi's, and newly built Lupe Tortilla and Ono Hawaiian BBQ). In-place economics as of 11/01/2026: **$5,025,763 of base rent ($17.71/SF) across 283,710 leased SF (93.6%)** plus **$5.72/SF of NNN recoveries**, producing the OM's stated **$4,646,126 in-place NOI**; year one of the projection (FY ending Oct-2027) carries $6,791,721 of effective gross revenue less $2,052,005 of operating expenses for $4,739,716. The trade area is the strongest in the library — **319,072 people within five miles at a $176,906 average household income**, **30.6% of households above $200,000**, 67.9% with a bachelor's degree and a $586,000 median home value — and DFW is currently the most active retail market in the country (2.9M SF of absorption over four quarters, NNN asking rents $21.59 and up 5.6% year over year). Density and income of that quality justify above-average rents and a tighter going-in cap. Newmark markets the asset as **34% below market on average**, and that number needs splitting before it is underwritten. Only **Petco (61% below market, NO remaining options, Feb-2029) and Pure Hockey (44% below, FMV option, Jan-2029)** actually reprice inside a normal hold — roughly **$360,000 of incremental NOI on $309,482 of current rent**. The rest of the gap is **locked behind fixed options**: HomeGoods holds three five-year options at $11.62-$12.62 against a $22.00 market into the 2040s, Total Wine two at $19.84/$21.83, Michaels one at $16.00 to Mar-2034, and PGA one at $9.08 to Oct-2036. That income is **secure, sticky and near-impossible to lose — but it is not capturable upside**, and the OM's own years 6-11 mark-to-market table ($860,000) sits outside a five-to-seven-year hold. Three things temper the going-in number. **$495,171 of modeled base rent (9.9%) comes from tenants that were not open and paying** at the analysis start — Lupe Tortilla and Ono Hawaiian BBQ were under construction and Joy Thai had not commenced — with the seller promising credits for gap rent. **PGA Tour Superstore is 21.6% of GLA and reports no sales at all**, so the largest single income concentration cannot be health-checked from the OM. And **Texas reassesses to market annually**: the 2025 assessed value is $56.0 million ($185/SF) against a 1.69% effective rate, while the model simply grows taxes 3% a year — a $75 million sale would imply roughly $1.27 million of tax versus the $965,743 underwritten, about 6% of NOI. Net: an irreplaceable Plano corner with real anchor productivity, ~$1.1 million of legitimate lease-up and mark-to-market, and a going-in NOI that should be re-cut for unopened tenants and a Texas tax reset before pricing.
keyAssumptions: Roster, in-place rents and recoveries come from the OM's Detailed Tenant Underwriting, stated as of the 11/01/2026 analysis start date. Every section of that schedule ties: SF, weighted-average base rent and NNN recovery reconcile exactly to the OM's printed subtotals for anchors, F&B, shops, limited-sales tenants and outparcels.

The `noi` field carries the OM's stated IN-PLACE NOI of $4,646,126 as of 11/01/2026. `effectiveGrossIncome` ($6,791,721) and `operatingExpenses` ($2,052,005) are the year-1 figures (fiscal year ending Oct-2027), which produce $4,739,716 — the $93,590 difference is contractual growth across year one.

The cash flow is an 11-year fiscal-year projection running Nov-2026 through Oct-2037. Three years show a $1 rounding difference between the OM's printed EGR less expenses and its printed NOI; the OM's own figures are carried unchanged.

INCOME NOT YET IN PLACE: the analysis assumes Lupe Tortilla (7,320 SF, under construction) and Ono Hawaiian BBQ (3,926 SF, under construction) are open and paying, and that Joy Thai (2,266 SF) is in place from the start date — $495,171 of base rent, 9.9% of the total. It also carries the Yoshi Shabu renewal (Mar-2027 to Feb-2032 at $42.00) and the Great Clips renewal (Jan-2027 to Dec-2031 at $31.00) as in-place. The seller is to credit gap rent and delivery costs in each case.

The analysis assumes PGA Tour Superstore renews at market with market TIs when its final option expires (Oct-2036), and that tenants holding FMV options priced 30% or more above their expiring rent roll to market rather than exercising.

Ten vacant suites totaling 19,283 SF are carried in the roster at $0 so roster SF ties to the 302,993 SF GLA. The OM's highlights describe the vacancy as 11 suites; the detailed underwriting lists 10.

Newmark's leasing assumptions: market rents set space-by-space (see each tenant's note), 3.0% general inflation / market-rent growth / expense growth, 5.0% general vacancy on potential gross rent excluding 11 named tenants, 75% renewal probability, 9-12 months downtime, TIs of $30-$40 PSF new and $0 renewal, commissions 6% new / 3% renewal, capital reserves $0.25 PSF, management fee 3% of effective gross revenue.

Real estate taxes: 2025 actual bill of $945,696 on $56,039,137 of assessed value across five parcels (four pads plus the main retail parcel), a 1.69% effective rate. The main retail parcel won an appeal that cuts its 2026 taxes 4%. The projection grows taxes 3% annually with NO sale-based reassessment — in Texas, where assessors mark to market annually and a sale is strong evidence of value, that step-up must be underwritten separately.

Tenant sales are the TTM figures from the detailed tenant underwriting (equal to the 2025 column for most tenants); 'health ratio' is used as the occupancy-cost ratio. The OM's earlier-year sales columns did not extract cleanly, so no prior-year trend is recorded. PGA Tour Superstore, HomeGoods, Petco and the limited-sales tenants report no sales at all.

Expense reimbursements are the OM's modeled year-1 NNN recovery per tenant. Per-lease recovery methodology lives in the Argus file in the deal folder (NMRK - Preston Village Center (2026)_.avux), not in the OM.
No asking price or cap rate is published in this OM, so price-based metrics are null.

redFlags.description: $495,171 of modeled base rent (9.9% of the total) comes from tenants that were NOT open and paying at the 11/01/2026 analysis start: Lupe Tortilla ($225,017) and Ono Hawaiian BBQ ($174,982) were under construction, and Joy Thai ($95,172) had not commenced. The OM promises seller credits for gap rent and delivery costs — quantify them and get them into the PSA, and re-cut going-in NOI without this income.

Texas tax reassessment is not modeled. The 2025 assessed value is $56,039,137 ($185/SF) with a $945,696 bill (1.69% effective), and the projection grows taxes only 3% a year. Texas assessors mark to market annually and a sale is the best evidence of value: at a $75 million price the bill runs roughly $1,267,500 versus the $965,743 underwritten in year one — about $300,000, or 6% of in-place NOI.

PGA Tour Superstore is 21.6% of GLA and the single largest income concentration, and it reports NO sales — the OM places it in a 'limited sales' group. Its lease expires Oct-2031 with one five-year option at a fixed $9.08/SF. The tenant's health cannot be tested from the OM; request sales before pricing the space.

The '34% below market' headline mixes capturable and locked rent. Only Petco (no options, Feb-2029) and Pure Hockey (FMV option, Jan-2029) actually reprice inside a normal hold, about $360,000. HomeGoods (three fixed options at $11.62-$12.62 vs a $22.00 market into the 2040s), Total Wine, Michaels (fixed $16.00 to Mar-2034) and PGA (fixed $9.08 to Oct-2036) are locked — that is secure, sticky income, not underwritable upside, and the OM's $860,000 years 6-11 table sits outside a five-to-seven-year hold.

Michaels is the weakest anchor on sales: $140 PSF at a 14.0% occupancy cost, roughly flat since 2023, on 7.8% of GLA. Its below-market $15.00/SF rent is what keeps the store viable, and a fixed $16.00 option runs to Mar-2034 — so there is no rent relief available if the tenant struggles, and no repricing if it stays.

A cluster of stressed small-shop tenants: Luckys Shoe Repair at a 68.1% occupancy cost, Pho Que Huong 18.8%, Aloha Poke Time 17.0%, Hi Sweetie 14.4% and Inchins Bamboo Garden 12.7%. With Michaels that is $621,519 of rent (12.4% of base) on tenants whose own sales do not comfortably support their rent, and four of the five roll by mid-2027.

Near-term rollover on a 4.1-year WALT: 20,054 SF and $541,731 of base rent (10.8%) expires by Oct-2027 across seven leases, and 134,325 SF — 44.3% of GLA — expires by Oct-2029. The 2029 cluster is where both the Petco/Pure Hockey upside and the largest re-leasing exposure sit.

Ono Hawaiian BBQ carries an $18.22/SF expense recovery, two to four times every other tenant in the center. Confirm it against the executed lease — a mis-keyed recovery on a new pad would overstate year-1 revenue by roughly $46,000.

OM typo: Lacrosse Unlimited's renewal options print as '2 x 5 @ $2.35 PSF, $2.66 PSF' against a $23.69/SF in-place rent. Those read as monthly figures (~$28.20 and ~$31.92 annually). Confirm the option economics from the lease.

McDonald's and the three other pads are separately parceled, which is what makes the outparcel spin-off possible — but pad leases of this vintage commonly carry a right of first refusal on a sale of the parcel. Confirm the ROFR position in each pad lease before underwriting a spin-off.

upsideItems.detail: 28,805 SF at a blended $10.74/SF against $22.89 market. Petco has NO remaining options and expires Feb-2029; Pure Hockey's single option is at FMV — so unlike the rest of the center's below-market rent, this actually reprices. The OM sizes it at roughly $360,000 of incremental NOI, against $309,482 of current base rent.

Ten suites of 1,167 to 3,009 SF against market rents averaging $39.22/SF, with absorption modeled May-2027 through Nov-2028 at $30-$35 PSF of TI. The OM sizes the stabilized pickup at roughly $760,000 of NOI — the single largest value-creation item in the deal.

Four separately parceled single-tenant pads (McDonald's, Dimassi's, Lupe Tortilla, Ono Hawaiian BBQ) totaling 25,755 SF and $742,821 of base rent can be sold individually at materially tighter cap rates than the center as a whole, returning capital while leaving the anchor income intact.

upsideItems.item: Exceptional trade area and market timing
upsideItems.detail: 319,072 residents within five miles at a $176,906 average household income, 30.6% of households above $200,000, 67.9% with a bachelor's degree, in the most active retail market in the United States (2.9M SF absorbed over four quarters, NNN asking rents up 5.6% to $21.59). High density plus high income is the profile that supports both premium rents and a tighter exit cap.

upsideItems.item: Durable anchor income at half of market rent
upsideItems.detail: HomeGoods at $11.12 (vs $22.00), PGA Tour Superstore at $8.25 (vs $15.00) and Total Wine at $18.04 (vs $22.00) are locked below market by fixed options. Not capturable — but a tenant does not walk away from rent this cheap, so this is the stickiest, lowest-vacancy-risk income in the center and it underpins the going-in yield.

The PGA of America's headquarters relocation to Frisco, 15 miles north, and the 2027 PGA Championship at PGA Frisco directly benefit the center's largest tenant, the #1 most-visited PGA Tour Superstore in Texas, which was remodeled in 2024.
